name: RM-Bench Chat
description: The chat domain split of RM-Bench (THU-KEG), evaluating reward models on their ability to distinguish subtle quality differences in conversational responses and their robustness to stylistic manipulations (verbosity, formatting, sycophancy). Tests whether chat-oriented reward models reward genuine helpfulness vs. surface-level style properties.
evaluation_method: reward model accuracy on subtle preference pairs; robustness to style perturbations (length, format, sycophancy)
general_score_metric: reward model accuracy on subtle chat preference pairs
typical_sota_score: ~60–75% accuracy on subtle quality pairs; style robustness varies widely across models
reputation: ICLR 2025 Oral; part of THU-KEG/RM-Bench; reveals that chat RMs disproportionately reward verbosity and formatting over genuine helpfulness; widely cited in reward-hacking literature
notes: ICLR 2025 Oral. Chat split of RM-Bench (THU-KEG/RM-Bench, arXiv:2410.16184). 183 instances. Each sample includes a chat prompt plus 3 chosen responses (concise, detailed plain, detailed markdown) and 3 rejected responses varying in style. Reveals systematic bias in chat reward models toward longer, formatted responses over correct, concise ones. Full benchmark: 1,381 total instances across chat (183), code (228), math (529), safety (441).
